layers.name: NDVI
layers.description: Measures vegetation health and density using the difference between near-infrared and red reflectance. Higher values indicate denser, healthier vegetation. Widely used for monitoring agricultural productivity, drought impacts, and ecosystem change.

layers.name: NDWI
layers.description: Detects surface water bodies and measures water content in vegetation using the difference between green and near-infrared bands. Positive values indicate open water surfaces. Essential for wetland monitoring and flood mapping.

layers.name: EVI
layers.description: Improved vegetation index that corrects for atmospheric and soil background effects. More sensitive than NDVI in areas of dense vegetation (high biomass). Reduces saturation effects in tropical and agricultural regions.

layers.name: MNDWI
layers.description: Enhanced water detection index using shortwave infrared instead of NIR. Better at distinguishing water from built-up areas and reduces noise from vegetation and soil. Preferred for urban wetland monitoring.

layers.name: NDMI
layers.description: Measures vegetation water content using NIR and SWIR bands. Sensitive to changes in leaf water content and soil moisture. Useful for detecting water stress in vegetation before visible symptoms appear.

layers.name: LST
layers.description: Surface temperature derived from thermal infrared bands. Indicates heat stress, urban heat island effects, and thermal characteristics of land cover types. Corrected for emissivity variations across different surfaces.

layers.name: TrueColor
layers.description: Natural color representation using Red, Green, and Blue bands. Shows the landscape as the human eye would see it. Useful for visual interpretation, land use mapping, and communicating changes to non-specialist audiences.

layers.name: FalseColor
layers.description: Near-infrared composite highlighting vegetation in red tones. Living vegetation appears bright red, water appears dark/black, and bare soil appears tan/brown. Standard composite for vegetation and water analysis.

layers.name: ET
layers.description: Actual evapotranspiration estimated from satellite thermal data and meteorological inputs. Represents water loss from soil evaporation and plant transpiration combined. Critical for water balance and irrigation management.
layers.bands: Derived from thermal, NDVI, and meteorological data

layers.name: Precipitation
layers.description: Annual accumulated precipitation from satellite and gauge-blended datasets. Provides spatial distribution of rainfall across the study area. Essential context for interpreting vegetation and water indices.
